verdict.rationale: Temporal supports automatic actions through code. Schedules start Workflow Executions at specified times and are more flexible than cron. Activities are retried automatically on failure, and Signals can be sent to running workflows to drive behavior. However, it is explicitly Workflows-as-Code rather than a rules engine, so event-driven triggering has to be written in SDK code instead of defined as rules. Missing for 10: declarative event-triggered rules, native external-event triggers (e.g. webhooks or event subscriptions starting workflows), a no-code rule definition surface, and independent corroboration of event-trigger use.
